module_title: The Atmosphere, Primary Pollutants, and Smog
introduction: Environmental chemistry is the study of chemical processes occurring in the environment and the impacts of human activities on them. At this level, we understand the main pollutants in the air and how they create hazardous 'Smog'.

core_concepts.title: Major Layers of the Atmosphere
core_concepts.description:
1. Troposphere: The lowest layer (0-10 km). All weather events happen here. This is where air pollution directly affects us. 
2. Stratosphere: Above the troposphere (10-50 km). This layer contains the 'Ozone Layer' which protects us from harmful Ultraviolet (UV) radiation.

core_concepts.title: Primary Pollutants
core_concepts.description:
Pollutants that are emitted directly from a source into the atmosphere. 
Examples: Carbon Monoxide ($CO$), Sulfur Dioxide ($SO_2$), Nitrogen Oxides ($NO_x$), and Particulate Matter (PM 2.5 and PM 10 from dust and soot).

core_concepts.title: Secondary Pollutants
core_concepts.description:
Pollutants that are NOT emitted directly. They form when primary pollutants undergo 'chemical reactions' in the atmosphere. 
Examples: Ozone ($O_3$ - when it forms in the troposphere), PAN (Peroxyacetyl Nitrate), and Acid Rain.

core_concepts.title: Smog (Smoke + Fog)
core_concepts.description:
1. Classical Smog (London Smog): Occurs in cool, humid climates. It is a mixture of smoke, fog, and Sulfur Dioxide ($SO_2$). 
2. Photochemical Smog (Los Angeles Smog): Occurs in warm, dry, sunny climates. Formed when sunlight (UV) reacts with Nitrogen Oxides ($NO_x$) and volatile organic compounds from vehicle exhaust. It appears as a 'Brown Haze'.

important_entities.name: The Danger of Carbon Monoxide ($CO$)
important_entities.key_fact: Reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood
important_entities.significance: $CO$ is a colorless, odorless gas produced by the incomplete combustion of fuels. It binds to the hemoglobin in our blood 300 times faster than oxygen does (forming Carboxyhemoglobin), which can lead to death by asphyxiation (suffocation).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Is Ozone a pollutant? Answer: In the 'Stratosphere', ozone is our 'Protector' (Good Ozone). But if it forms in the 'Troposphere' (the air we breathe), it is highly toxic and acts as a dangerous 'Pollutant' (Bad Ozone).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Whenever an exam asks 'Which of the following is a secondary pollutant?', blindly look for PAN or Ozone ($O_3$) in the options.

exam_strategy_tips: A frequently asked SSC question: 'Why is it dangerous to sleep in a closed room with a burning coal fire?' Answer: Because incomplete combustion produces deadly 'Carbon Monoxide' ($CO$) gas.
